acceptance.output_evidence:
THE READING, WITH NO VERDICT ON IT.
(1) WHAT THE SWEEP NOW MEASURES. Two TYPE SCOPES on ONE served graph, under ONE vintage. It used to be two SURFACES -- two different graphs, two different freshness stories, one statement stretched across both and the type filter done in Python afterwards. Now each scope names itself in its own Cypher and the union is a dedup, not a reconciliation. Live: nessie 308 isolates, stitch 207 of 1,674 stitch-typed nodes, union 515, 384 suppressed and logged, 131 real orphans, 1,133 function-granular gold sub-nodes dropped as isolated-by-design.
(2) WHAT IT LOST, AND WHETHER THE REPLACEMENT IS ADEQUATE. It lost a 48-hour bar that REFUSED. That bar existed for the D1 592-hour-stale finding: a sweep over a stale surface phantoms orphans, because a 0-edge node is indistinguishable from a node whose edges were not rebuilt. The replacement is the served VINTAGE line, and the honest answer is that it is adequate for a DIFFERENT reason than the bar was, not a like-for-like swap. The bar was a REFUSAL -- it stopped the scan. The vintage line is a DISCLOSURE -- it labels the answer and trusts the reader. What makes that trade sound here is that the failure mode the bar guarded against cannot occur the same way: a served projection is swapped atomically behind a pointer, so what is served IS a coherent generation, and there is no BEHIND state in which a caller silently reads yesterday's edges. What the vintage line does NOT do is stop a reader who does not look. A reader who takes 131 orphans and never reads the line above them can still be reading a graph built from a stitch that failed last night -- which is the residual risk, and it is why the line is printed once for BOTH legs, on the family's own row, from the response that produced those very counts rather than from a health call at another moment.
(3) WHAT THE DELTA SAYS. +96 residuals, 112 of them keys the baseline never held, overwhelmingly GOLD_SCRIPT and S3_DATA_KEY. That is not a regression and it is not really a measurement of the estate either: it is the difference between two universes. The baseline was established against kuzu_nessie_db plus a July local stitch store; this run reads the September served graph whose stitch layer was folded in hours ago by CG-s-24. The July store's stitch was a frozen local projection of a graph nobody was maintaining -- that is why CG-s-20 declared it interim and why _stitch_freshness refused on it. So the delta is best read as: the stitch scope has moved from a stale private copy to a fresh shared one, and 112 orphans that were invisible or differently-named in July are now visible under the interim stitch-v1 vocabulary. Two consequences a grader should weigh. First, the alarm now fires 112 times on every run, and a standing alarm that always fires is an alarm that stops being read -- so this needs a decision, not a shrug. Second, whatever is decided will need doing TWICE unless it waits: S31 (TO-CG-F-11) renames GOLD_SCRIPT into PipelineScript/PipelineFunction and merges S3_DATA_KEY into S3Key, which will change every one of these residual KEYS again, because a key is family::class/deviation::sites and the class is the node_type. Re-establishing the baseline today buys a quiet scan for exactly as long as it takes F-11 to land.
(4) WHAT THIS ORDER DID NOT DECIDE. It did not touch the baseline, did not run --establish-baseline (that flag REWRITES the CVO's file), and did not change the family registry's stale 'pending' declaration (row W2-S59). The store's bytes are untouched and merely unread; CG-s-26 retires them.
